public_rationale: On November 10, 2025, TechCrunch reported Gamma's founder saying the AI startup had profitably reached $100 million in annual recurring revenue [e1]. This challenges the claim that every AI startup loses millions annually, but the report does not specify Gamma's full-year 2025 net income or the accounting basis for profitability [e1]. It therefore does not establish a comparable annual counterexample, and it supplies neither accounts for the whole startup population nor separate cash-flow evidence [e1]. The universal annual-loss claim remains unresolved [e1].
limitations: Gamma's profitability statement does not identify the profit measure or reporting period.
Annual recurring revenue does not establish realized annual revenue or net income.
The evidence does not establish whether startups have found economically durable ways to stop consuming cash.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Every AI startup loses millions or billions of dollars a year and none appears to have found a way to stop.

statement.excerpt: Every AI startup loses millions or billions of dollars a year, and nobody appears to have worked out a way to stop hemorrhaging cash.

from_speaker: loses millions or billions of dollars a year
nobody appears to have worked out a way to stop hemorrhaging cash
our_interpretation: Read “every” literally, including AI application startups as well as foundation-model developers.
Read annual losses as company-wide annual net losses; assess cash consumption separately because it is not the same measure.
Use calendar 2025, the latest completed calendar year before the post, as the common annual comparison period. Differing fiscal years require explicit reconciliation.
Treat “millions” as losses of at least $2 million for a numerical test; a profitable or break-even startup is a counterexample under any ordinary reading of that threshold.
No cited accounting convention accompanies this assertion. Its accounting basis remains unknown.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable annual accounts establish losses of at least millions of dollars for every qualifying startup in the target population, with separate evidence for continuing cash consumption.
criteria.contradiction_condition: One qualifying startup has a profitable or break-even target year, or an annual loss demonstrably below the claimed magnitude, on a compatible accounting basis.
